instructions: Write as if the Polish product were created in Poland from the beginning.
Preserve mechanics, facts, character roles, safety and claim boundaries.
Use contemporary Polish book language: natural, not chatty or telegraphic.
Breath/reset units must use concrete everyday framing, never imported mindfulness/wellness language.
Activity instructions must be complete enough to perform from Polish alone.
Keep Happy Makers humor strong, Polish-first and character-specific.

units.function: Use one minute of pulse/body awareness as a concrete pause without mystical shared-heart framing.
mechanics: Sit together.
Each person places a hand on own chest/heart area.
Notice own pulse.
Stay with the sensation for about one minute.
safety_claim_boundaries: Do not claim all hearts literally synchronize.
Do not turn pulse awareness into a medical claim.
units.humor_room: Nini can joke about hearts doing their own job.

units.function: Build a cumulative one-word story, then replay the same story using movements or sounds instead of the words.
mechanics: Oldest person starts with one word.
Next person repeats all previous words in order and adds one new word.
Continue around circle for only 2-3 rounds to create a short story.
Then retell the same story again.
On the retelling, each person replaces their own word with a movement or sound representing it.
immutable_facts: Same story is replayed with movement/sound substitutions.
character_roles: Alio is energetic and encourages absurdity.
units.tone_job: Clear cumulative-memory game followed by physical/sound replay.

units.function: Pass one specific thank-you around the circle until everyone receives at least one.
mechanics: Youngest person starts.
Starter turns to person on their right.
Say 'thank you for...' and name one specific thing that person did for them or the family.
Continue around until each person has received at least one thank-you message.
immutable_facts: Everyone receives at least one message.
character_roles: Luli keeps it sincere but unsentimental.

units.function: Pair several calm breaths with one concrete grateful thought, replacing golden-light visualization with everyday framing.
mechanics: Sit together.
Take several unforced breaths.
On an inhale, recall one concrete good thing/person from today.
On an exhale, let shoulders/body soften rather than performing a visualization.
safety_claim_boundaries: Do not claim breath/light connects people or guarantees calm.
units.tone_job: Gratitude plus breath without wellness language.
units.humor_room: Luli can joke about not needing special effects.
units.cultural_friction: Replace golden-light metaphor with a concrete remembered moment.

units.function: Run the Human Knot with full hand-selection and untangling mechanics plus two-person variant.
mechanics: Stand close in a circle.
Each person reaches across and takes the hands of two different people.
Do not take the hands of immediate neighbors.
Without releasing hands, work together to untangle into one open circle.
Two-person variant: stand face to face, cross arms to hold hands, then slowly untwist together while keeping eye contact.
immutable_facts: Hands belong to two different non-neighbors.
safety_claim_boundaries: Move gently; no painful twisting or forced joints.

units.function: Name one small good thing from family life today without spiritual 'blessing' language.
mechanics: Each person names one small thing from family life today that they are genuinely glad happened or existed.
character_roles: Luli grounds sentiment in everyday details.

units.function: Create a shoulder-to-shoulder breathing pause without river/flow metaphors.
mechanics: Sit shoulder to shoulder.
Take several comfortable breaths.
Notice own inhale/exhale while remaining physically near the group.
character_roles: Alio is team-minded and lightly comic.
safety_claim_boundaries: No claim breath travels between people or carries calm.
units.humor_room: Alio can joke about everyone finally moving at one speed.

units.function: Build a cumulative family robot-machine sequence of movement+sound and perform it together at the end.
mechanics: Starter is person whose name begins with the letter closest to beginning of alphabet.
Starter makes one robot-like movement plus one sound.
Next person repeats starter movement+sound and adds own movement+sound.
Each following person repeats full sequence in order and adds one new robot action.
At end whole family performs entire robot-machine sequence together in sync.
immutable_facts: Movement and sound as a pair.
units.humor_room: Dilo can treat errors like software bugs.

units.function: Create one short family motto that actually sounds usable rather than sentimental.
mechanics: Together invent one short sentence that describes your family's spirit/way of being.
Keep it short and memorable.
Examples may be culturally rewritten.
immutable_facts: Dilo compares short motto to a strong password.
safety_claim_boundaries: Do not force values language or make the family adopt a solemn slogan.

units.function: Use a tiny facial relaxation/smile pause rather than 'inner smile changes room energy'.
mechanics: Sit close together.
Close eyes.
Let face relax.
Form a small, comfortable smile for a few breaths.
Remain quiet briefly, then finish.
safety_claim_boundaries: Do not claim smiles alter room energy or mood for everyone.
units.humor_room: Nini can joke about suspiciously quiet smiling.

units.function: Execute a three-part weird command game with movement+sound+face, leader chosen by colorful socks, and leader change on hesitation/laughter/slowness.
mechanics: Leader is person wearing most colorful socks today.
Leader gives a command with exactly 3 parts: movement + sound + facial expression.
Everyone, including leader, immediately performs full combination at same time.
Use several rounds.
Whoever hesitates, laughs or reacts too slowly becomes next leader.

units.function: Complete 'Our family is really good at...' in turns, keeping the idea playful and concrete.
mechanics: Take turns finishing sentence 'Our family is really good at...' with one specific strength/skill/habit.
immutable_facts: Alio jokes every family has a superpower.
units.cultural_friction: Avoid grand 'shared strengths bring pride' language.

units.function: Pair one breath and a brief look at each other with a concrete private appreciation thought.
mechanics: Sit together.
Take one comfortable breath.
Open eyes slowly.
Look at one another briefly.
Silently think of one specific thing you appreciate about the person/people you see.
safety_claim_boundaries: Do not require intense eye contact or emotional display.

units.function: Run exact-five-word clue game: 3 true clues, 2 absurd lies, identify lies then character, moving anticlockwise.
mechanics: Starter is person with longest middle/second name.
Starter silently chooses any recognizable character/object/animal/hero/fairy-tale figure.
Describe it using exactly five words.
Exactly 3 words are true clues and 2 are absurd lies.
Family first guesses which two words are lies.
Then family guesses final character/object.
Move anticlockwise for next rounds.
immutable_facts: Starter based on longest second name.
character_roles: Luli likes logic mixed with nonsense.
units.humor_room: Luli can defend nonsense as methodology.

units.function: Name one kind thing recently noticed in the person to your left; continue clockwise until everyone has spoken.
mechanics: First person turns to person on their left.
Name one kind thing noticed that person did recently, even something small.
Continue clockwise until all members have shared feedback.
immutable_facts: Direction starts left then continues clockwise.
character_roles: Mimi jokes kindness grows faster than laundry, almost.
safety_claim_boundaries: Keep feedback kind and concrete; no forced disclosure.

units.function: Use one minute of slow hand movement and noticing air resistance without mindfulness jargon.
mechanics: For one minute, raise hands together very slowly.
Lower/move them slowly again.
Notice air against skin while moving.
units.humor_room: Dilo can joke about loading speed.

units.function: Create a kindness doorway with two raised arms; each person passes through while others say kind words; preserve two-person chair variant.
mechanics: Two family members raise arms to make doorway.
One person walks slowly through.
Other family members quietly say kind words about that person while they pass.
Rotate roles until everyone has passed through.
Two-person variant: use two chairs as doorway, take turns walking through while saying kind words to each other.
safety_claim_boundaries: Use safe stable chairs; no forced touching.

units.function: Each person names one real 'family treasure' the family shares, using concrete examples rather than abstract richness claims.
mechanics: Imagine family as a map with treasures.
Each person names one treasure the family has.
Treasure may be concrete or relational: shared humor, help, trust, routines, support, etc.
units.tone_job: Light metaphor anchored in real family assets.
units.cultural_friction: Avoid 'see how rich we are' language.

units.function: Use warm palms and optional shoulder touch as a concrete sensory pause; remove 'warmth travels between you'.
mechanics: Rub palms together until warm.
Rest one hand on own chest.
Place other hand gently on shoulder of person to right if they want contact.
Stay still briefly and notice warmth in hands.
immutable_facts: Other hand on right person's shoulder.
safety_claim_boundaries: Do not claim warmth/comfort literally transfers between people.
units.humor_room: Luli can joke hands finally have a job.

units.function: Pass short rhythms clockwise, repeating each exactly, then perform every person's rhythm sequence from start to finish together.
mechanics: Shortest person starts with one simple tapped/clapped rhythm.
Everyone repeats it exactly.
Move clockwise; next person invents a new short rhythm.
Everyone repeats each new rhythm.
Continue until everyone created one rhythm.
Challenge: perform the entire sequence of everyone's rhythms from start to finish together.
character_roles: Dilo allows creative interpretation while keeping rhythm.

units.function: Pass one specific appreciation to the person on the left in a simple circle.
mechanics: First person turns to person on their left.
Say one short specific thing they appreciate about that person.
Continue around so the same pattern reaches everyone.
